page: Amazon Web Services r5b.2xlarge is a memory-optimized fifth-generation instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz. The configuration includes 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a mixture of average and weak performance profiles. The processor delivers average multi-core performance in stress-ng and Passmark CPU tests, though single-core metrics in Geekbench and stress-ng fall into the lower tier. Memory bandwidth is stable, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 376.63 GB/sec and large block uncached write speeds at 32.96 GB/sec. Redis SET operations perform at an average rate of 6.89 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput reaches 7.1 GB/sec.

The r5b.2xlarge offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require high-performance single-core compute or local SSD storage. However, the lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, and the weak single-threaded performance in compression and decompression tasks represents a notable tradeoff. This instance is best suited for in-memory databases, caching layers like Redis, software compilation, and moderate web serving workloads.
